user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.\nDaisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"\nAssistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.\nDaisy: "Please review PR #1234"\nAssistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.\nDaisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"\nAssistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)
- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

1	/*

     7	import React from 'react'
     8	import {FormattedMessage, FormattedNumber} from 'react-intl'
     9	import {
    10	    Box,
    11	    Flex,
    12	    Button,
    13	    Stack,
    14	    Text,
    15	    Heading,
    16	    Divider,
    17	    Accordion,
    18	    AccordionIcon,
    19	    AccordionItem,
    20	    AccordionButton,
    21	    AccordionPanel
    22	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
    23	import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link'
    24	import {PromoCode, usePromoCode} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/promo-code'
    25	import ItemVariantProvider from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant'
    26	import CartItemVariantImage from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-image'
    27	import CartItemVariantName from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-name'
    28	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes'
    29	import CartItemVariantPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price'
    30	import PromoPopover from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/promo-popover'
    31	import {useProducts} from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react'
    32	import type {ShopperBasketsTypes} from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic'
    33	import {BasketIcon} from '../icons'
    34	import {consolidateDuplicateBonusProducts} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/bonus-product/cart'
    35	
    36	
    37	// Narrowed from ShopperBasketsTypes.PriceAdjustment: only the three fields this component reads.
    38	// appliedDiscount and discount-type logic are omitted by design — the display format is always
    39	// "{promotion_name} Applied" regardless of promotion type.
    40	type OrderPriceAdjustment = Pick<ShopperBasketsTypes.PriceAdjustment, 'priceAdjustmentId' | 'itemText' | 'price'>
    41	
    42	// BasketProp is kept as a local narrowed type because this component renders both baskets
    43	// (basketId) and orders (orderNo), and no single SDK type covers both response shapes.
    44	type BasketProp = {
    45	    basketId?: string
    46	    orderNo?: string
    47	    currency?: string
    48	    productSubTotal?: number
    49	    orderTotal?: number
    50	    productTotal?: number
    51	    shippingTotal?: number | null
    52	    taxTotal?: number | null
    53	    productItems?: ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem[]
    54	    orderPriceAdjustments?: OrderPriceAdjustment[]
    55	    shippingItems?: ShopperBasketsTypes.ShippingItem[]
    56	    couponItems?: ShopperBasketsTypes.CouponItem[]
    57	}
    58	
    59	type CartItemsProps = {
    60	    basket: BasketProp
    61	}
    62	
    63	const CartItems = ({basket}: CartItemsProps) => {
    64	    const totalItems = basket?.productItems?.reduce((acc: number, item: ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem) => acc + (item.quantity ?? 0), 0) || 0
    65	    const productIds = basket?.productItems?.map((item: ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem) => item.productId).join(',') ?? ''
    66	    const {data: products} = useProducts(
    67	        {
    68	            parameters: {
    69	                // SDK type expects string[] but the base component passes a comma-joined string — runtime behaviour is correct
    70	                ids: productIds as unknown as string[],
    71	                // allImages is still required (not just expand:['images']) so the image group for the
    72	                // cart item's actual selected variant is included, not just the default representative one.
    73	                allImages: true,
    74	                // Narrow expand from the full default set (prices, availability, promotions, options,
    75	                // set_products, recommendations, shipping_methods, page_meta_tags) to only what
    76	                // CartItemVariantImage/Name/Attributes/Price read from the product.
    77	                expand: ['images', 'variations'],
    78	                // Scoped to the fields those four components read, and the imageGroups filtered to the
    79	                // 'small' viewType CartItemVariantImage looks up — the smallest supported image
    80	                // expansion that still lets findImageGroupBy match the purchased variant's colour.
    81	                select: '(data.(id,name,master.(masterId),type.(bundle,master,set),c_isSale,variationAttributes.(id,name,values.(value,name)),imageGroups[viewType=small].(viewType,images.(link,disBaseLink,alt),variationAttributes.(id,values.(value)))))'
    82	            }
    83	        },
    84	        {
    85	            enabled: Boolean(productIds),
    86	            // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
    87	            select: (result: any) => {
    88	                // Index products by id for O(1) lookup when building variant objects below.
    89	                return result?.data?.reduce((acc: Record<string, unknown>, item: {id: string}) => {
    90	                    acc[item.id] = item
    91	                    return acc
    92	                }, {})
    93	            }
    94	        }
    95	    )
    96	
    97	    return (
    98	        <Accordion allowToggle={true} width="100%">
    99	            <AccordionItem style={{border: 0}}>
   100	                <AccordionButton color="blue.700">
   101	                    <BasketIcon aria-hidden={true} />
   102	                    <Box px={2}>
   103	                        <FormattedMessage
   104	                            id="order_summary.cart_items.action.num_of_items_in_cart"
   105	                            description="clicking it would expand/show the items in cart"
   106	                            defaultMessage="{itemCount, plural, =0 {0 items} one {# item} other {# items}} in cart"
   107	                            values={{itemCount: totalItems}}
   108	                        />
   109	                    </Box>
   110	                    <AccordionIcon />
   111	                </AccordionButton>
   112	                <AccordionPanel px={0} py={4}>
   113	                    <Stack spacing={5} align="flex-start" divider={<Divider />}>
   114	                        {(() => {
   115	                            const consolidatedItems = consolidateDuplicateBonusProducts(
   116	                                basket.productItems || []
   117	                            )
   118	                            return consolidatedItems.map((product: ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem, idx: number) => {
   119	                                const variant = {
   120	                                    ...product,
   121	                                    ...((products as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.[product.productId ?? ''] ?? {}),
   122	                                    price: product.price
   123	                                }
   124	                                return (
   125	                                    <ItemVariantProvider
   126	                                        key={`order-summary-item-${product.productId ?? ''}-${
   127	                                            product.itemId || idx
   128	                                        }`}
   129	                                        index={idx}
   130	                                        variant={variant}
   131	                                    >
   132	                                        <Flex width="full" alignItems="flex-start">
   133	                                            <CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />
   134	                                            <Stack width="full" spacing={1} marginTop="-3px">
   135	                                                <CartItemVariantName />
   136	                                                <CartItemVariantAttributes includeQuantity />
   137	                                                <CartItemVariantPrice
   138	                                                    baseDirection="row"
   139	                                                    currency={basket?.currency}
   140	                                                />
   141	                                            </Stack>
   142	                                        </Flex>
   143	                                    </ItemVariantProvider>
   144	                                )
   145	                            })
   146	                        })()}
   147	
   148	                        <Button as={Link} to="/cart" variant="link" width="full" color="blue.700">
   149	                            <FormattedMessage
   150	                                defaultMessage="Edit cart"
   151	                                id="order_summary.cart_items.link.edit_cart"
   152	                            />
   153	                        </Button>
   154	                    </Stack>
   155	                </AccordionPanel>
   156	            </AccordionItem>
   157	        </Accordion>
   158	    )
   159	}
   160	
   161	type OrderSummaryProps = {
   162	    basket: BasketProp
   163	    showPromoCodeForm?: boolean
   164	    showCartItems?: boolean
   165	    isEstimate?: boolean
   166	    fontSize?: 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl'
   167	}
   168	
   169	const OrderSummary = ({
   170	    basket,
   171	    showPromoCodeForm = false,
   172	    showCartItems = false,
   173	    isEstimate = false,
   174	    fontSize = 'md'
   175	}: OrderSummaryProps) => {
   176	    const {removePromoCode, ...promoCodeProps} = usePromoCode()
   177	
   178	    if (!basket?.basketId && !basket?.orderNo) {
   179	        return null
   180	    }
   181	    // Aggregate price adjustments across every shipment, not just the first — a multi-shipment
   182	    // basket can have shipping promotions on shipment 2+ that shippingItems[0] alone would miss.
   183	    const shippingPriceAdjustments =
   184	        basket.shippingItems?.flatMap((item) =>
   185	            (item.priceAdjustments ?? []).map((adjustment) => ({...adjustment, shipmentId: item.shipmentId}))
   186	        ) ?? []
   187	    const hasShippingPromos = shippingPriceAdjustments.length > 0
   188	
   189	    return (
   190	        <Stack data-testid="sf-order-summary" spacing={5}>
   191	            <Heading fontSize={fontSize} pt={1} id="order-summary-heading">
   192	                <FormattedMessage
   193	                    defaultMessage="Order Summary"
   194	                    id="order_summary.heading.order_summary"
   195	                />
   196	            </Heading>
   197	
   198	            <Stack
   199	                spacing={4}
   200	                align="flex-start"
   201	                role="region"
   202	                aria-labelledby="order-summary-heading"
   203	            >
   204	                {showCartItems && <CartItems basket={basket} />}
   205	
   206	                <Stack w="full">
   207	                    <Flex justify="space-between" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
   208	                        <Text fontWeight="bold" fontSize={fontSize}>
   209	                            <FormattedMessage
   210	                                defaultMessage="Subtotal"
   211	                                id="order_summary.label.subtotal"
   212	                            />
   213	                        </Text>
   214	                        <Text fontWeight="bold" fontSize={fontSize}>
   215	                            <FormattedNumber
   216	                                style="currency"
   217	                                currency={basket?.currency}
   218	                                value={basket?.productSubTotal ?? 0}
   219	                            />
   220	                        </Text>
   221	                    </Flex>
   222	
   223	                    {/* Order-level promotions (e.g. VIC 20% member discount) are rendered as
   224	                        "{promotion_name} Applied" with the adjustment amount in green.
   225	                        No discount-type branching — the format is the same for all promotion types. */}
   226	                    {basket.orderPriceAdjustments?.map((adjustment: OrderPriceAdjustment) => (
   227	                        <Flex
   228	                            justify="space-between"
   229	                            key={adjustment.priceAdjustmentId}
   230	                            aria-live="polite"
   231	                            aria-atomic="true"
   232	                        >
   233	                            <Text fontSize={fontSize}>
   234	                                {adjustment.itemText}{' '}
   235	                                <FormattedMessage
   236	                                    defaultMessage="Applied"
   237	                                    id="order_summary.label.promotion_applied_suffix"
   238	                                />
   239	                            </Text>
   240	                            <Text color="green.600" fontSize={fontSize}>
   241	                                <FormattedNumber
   242	                                    style="currency"
   243	                                    currency={basket?.currency}
   244	                                    value={adjustment.price ?? 0}
   245	                                />
   246	                            </Text>
   247	                        </Flex>
   248	                    ))}
   249	
   250	                    <Flex justify="space-between" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
   251	                        <Flex alignItems="center">
   252	                            <Text lineHeight={1} fontSize={fontSize}>
   253	                                <FormattedMessage
   254	                                    defaultMessage="Shipping"
   255	                                    id="order_summary.label.shipping"
   256	                                />
   257	                                {hasShippingPromos && (
   258	                                    <Text as="span" ml={1}>
   259	                                        (
   260	                                        <FormattedMessage
   261	                                            defaultMessage="Promotion applied"
   262	                                            id="order_summary.label.promo_applied"
   263	                                        />
   264	                                        )
   265	                                    </Text>
   266	                                )}
   267	                            </Text>
   268	                            {hasShippingPromos && (
   269	                                <PromoPopover ml={1}>
   270	                                    <Stack>
   271	                                        {shippingPriceAdjustments.map((adjustment, index) => (
   272	                                            <Text
   273	                                                key={`${adjustment.shipmentId ?? 'shipment'}-${
   274	                                                    adjustment.priceAdjustmentId ?? index
   275	                                                }`}
   276	                                                fontSize="sm"
   277	                                            >
   278	                                                {adjustment.itemText}
   279	                                            </Text>
   280	                                        ))}
   281	                                    </Stack>
   282	                                </PromoPopover>
   283	                            )}
   284	                        </Flex>
   285	
   286	                        {basket.shippingTotal === 0 ? (
   287	                            <Text
   288	                                as="span"
   289	                                color="green.700"
   290	                                textTransform="uppercase"
   291	                                fontSize={fontSize}
   292	                            >
   293	                                <FormattedMessage
   294	                                    defaultMessage="Free"
   295	                                    id="order_summary.label.free"
   296	                                />
   297	                            </Text>
   298	                        ) : basket.shippingTotal != null ? (
   299	                            <Text fontSize={fontSize}>
   300	                                <FormattedNumber
   301	                                    value={basket.shippingTotal}
   302	                                    style="currency"
   303	                                    currency={basket.currency}
   304	                                />
   305	                            </Text>
   306	                        ) : (
   307	                            <Text fontSize={fontSize} color="gray.700">
   308	                                <FormattedMessage
   309	                                    defaultMessage="TBD"
   310	                                    id="order_summary.label.shipping_tbd"

1	import React from 'react';
     2	import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
     3	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
     4	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
     5	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
     6	import { MultiSiteProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
     7	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
     8	import OrderSummary from './index';
     9	
    10	// OrderSummary calls usePromoCode() unconditionally (even with showPromoCodeForm off), which
    11	// calls useCurrentBasket() -> useSFPayments() -> useAppOrigin() -> useOrigin() — the same chain
    12	// documented at header/index.stories.tsx, needing the identical provider stack for the same
    13	// reason: ServerContext has no default value, so the unconditional `{res}` destructure inside
    14	// useOrigin throws without a provider, regardless of environment. disableAuthInit means no real
    15	// SFCC auth call fires, and usePromoCode's own basket resolves to undefined here — harmless,
    16	// since this component's own basket data always comes from the `basket` prop below, not from
    17	// usePromoCode's internal fetch.
    18	const storybookQueryClient = new QueryClient({
    19	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
    20	});
    21	
    22	const meta: Meta<typeof OrderSummary> = {
    23	  title: 'Commerce/OrderSummary',
    24	  component: OrderSummary,
    25	  decorators: [
    26	    (Story) => (
    27	      <ServerContext.Provider value={{}}>
    28	        <MemoryRouter>
    29	          <MultiSiteProvider
    30	            site={{ id: 'ZimmermannAU', alias: 'au' }}
    31	            locale={{ id: 'en-AU', alias: 'en-AU' }}
    32	            buildUrl={(path: string) => path}
    33	          >
    34	            <QueryClientProvider client={storybookQueryClient}>
    35	              <CommerceApiProvider
    36	                clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    37	                organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
    38	                shortCode="storybook"
    39	                siteId="ZimmermannAU"
    40	                locale="en-AU"
    41	                currency="AUD"
    42	                proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
    43	                redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
    44	                disableAuthInit
    45	                silenceWarnings
    46	              >
    47	                <Story />
    48	              </CommerceApiProvider>
    49	            </QueryClientProvider>
    50	          </MultiSiteProvider>
    51	        </MemoryRouter>
    52	      </ServerContext.Provider>
    53	    ),
    54	  ],
    55	};
    56	
    57	export default meta;
    58	type Story = StoryObj<typeof OrderSummary>;
    59	
    60	const baseBasket = {
    61	  basketId: 'storybook-basket-id',
    62	  currency: 'AUD',
    63	  productSubTotal: 120,
    64	  orderTotal: 130,
    65	  shippingTotal: 10,
    66	  taxTotal: 0,
    67	};
    68	
    69	/** Baseline — single shipment, no promotions, a real shipping charge. */
    70	export const Default: Story = {
    71	  args: {
    72	    basket: baseBasket,
    73	  },
    74	};
    75	
    76	/**
    77	 * A promotion applied only to the second shipment (e.g. a multiship order) — the "Promotion
    78	 * applied" label and popover must reflect it even though shipment 1 has none of its own.
    79	 * Regression coverage for the CodeRabbit finding: this used to read `shippingItems[0]` only.
    80	 */

    82	  args: {
    83	    basket: {
    84	      ...baseBasket,
    85	      shippingItems: [
    86	        { shipmentId: 'shipment-1', priceAdjustments: [] },
    87	        {
    88	          shipmentId: 'shipment-2',
    89	          priceAdjustments: [
    90	            { priceAdjustmentId: 'promo-shipment-2', itemText: 'Free shipping (shipment 2)', price: -10 },
    91	          ],
    92	        },
    93	      ],
    94	    },
    95	  },
    96	};
    97	
    98	/** shippingTotal === 0 — the "Free" label, not a formatted $0.00. */
    99	export const FreeShipping: Story = {
   100	  args: {

   102	  },

+ * pricing, taking into account applied discounts as well as base item prices.

+    const isMaster = (variant?.type as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.master as boolean | undefined

+

PR 118 | feat(sfcc-645/sfcc-778): cart and catalogue price rule, display Was/Now pricing in cart, order summary and PDP size selection
author: joselitopperezjr-acn | head: feature/SFCC-778_customer-group-pricing-catalogue-price-rule-display -> base: develop
reviewRequests: ['PWA Squad B', 'PWA Squad A']
latestReviews: [('coderabbitai', 'DISMISSED'), ('bryanian09', 'DISMISSED')]
--- BODY ---
# Description

Delivers SFCC-645 (cart item Was/Now pricing and order-level promotion display in order summary) and SFCC-778 (catalogue price rule display — PDP Was/Now correctly scoped to the selected size).

**Cart Was/Now (SFCC-645).** The base SFCC `item-price` component renders a flat price with no awareness of order-level promotions (e.g. VIC 20% member discount applied server-side). This override reads `priceAfterOrderDiscount` first, then `priceAfterItemDiscount`, as the effective current price and delegates the Was/Now label rendering to `ZimmProductPrice` — the same atom already used on PLP and PDP — rather than duplicating the label strings and styling.

**Order summary promotion display (SFCC-645).** The base `order-summary` renders promotion adjustments with discount-type branching logic (percentage vs fixed-amount). This override simplifies that to a flat `{promotion_name} Applied` format with the adjustment amount shown in green — no type detection, matching the confirmed AC.

**PDP Was/Now on size selection (SFCC-194/SFCC-778).** Was/Now was silently suppressed after a shopper picked a size. Root cause: `product-view` stores the selected size in local React state (`localSizeValue`) and never writes it to the URL, so `urlPid` was always `undefined` after a size pick — `selectVariantScopedPriceData` received no pid, fell back to colour-only (range) pricing, and correctly suppressed Was/Now for a range. Fix: `onVariationChange` on the standalone `ProductView` captures the selected size into `selectedSizeSelection` (stored as a `{ colour, size }` pair so a stale size from the previous colour can never resolve on the same render that `urlColour` changes). `pricingVariantId` is then derived by matching colour+size against the master's `variants[]`, giving `selectVariantScopedPriceData` a real pid to narrow on.

# Linked

- Tickets: **SFCC-645** (cart item price and order summary promotion display), **SFCC-778** (catalogue price rule display), **SFCC-194** (PDP Was/Now)
- Design: Zimmermann_Designs Figma file — PDP/Cart/Order Summary price treatment

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad A

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] **Bug fix** (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

# Changes

- `components/item-variant/item-price.tsx` (new override) — reads `priceAfterOrderDiscount` then `priceAfterItemDiscount` as the effective price; delegates Was/Now rendering to `ZimmProductPrice`; falls back to `DisplayPrice` when no discount applies or no `itemId` is present (wishlist path)
- `components/order-summary/index.tsx` (new override, **Tier 2**) — simplified `OrderPriceAdjustment` type with `appliedDiscount` and discount-type branching removed; renders each order adjustment as `{promotion_name} Applied` with the amount in green via `FormattedMessage` (i18n-ready, key `order_summary.label.promotion_applied_suffix`)
- `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — adds `selectedSizeSelection` state captu

content.content:
=== pricing-currency-globale.md §3 + §5 (PRC-09, PRC-17..19) ===

---

## 3. Sale & Markdown Pricing (PRC-09 – PRC-13)

- Original list price displayed alongside active sale price — shown on PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, and order history. Note (DR): sale items are usually excluded from recommendations via a manual rule (PRC-09)
- Business users can schedule sale pricing to go live at a specified future date and time. Category pre-merchandised; team QCs via live-preview before go-live (PRC-10, confirmed)
- **SFCC native storefront preview** supports QC of scheduled pricing and category changes before go-live, including preview for specific customer groups — scoped to SFCC OOTB preview, no custom build (PRC-11, confirmed)
- Final sale flag supported on products (PRC-12, confirmed). Assumption: `is_returnable` drives returnable status, `final_sale` drives front-end final-sale messaging. Attribute distinction and AP21 derivation still to be confirmed — see Open Items. No final-sale icon in design yet
- Price display behaviour based on AP21 `MarkdownStatus` values (permanent / temporary / temppermanent) — open: Zimmermann to confirm what each value means and what storefront behaviour it should drive (PRC-13, open)

---

## 4. Multi-Currency & Regional Pricebooks (PRC-14, PRC-36 – PRC-43, PRC-47 – PRC-52)

- Country/currency selector shows prices in the currency configured for the customer's selected shipping country (PRC-14, confirmed). Note (RJ): the country selector is not present on the AU site
- **Country-to-currency mapping** configurable in SFCC Business Manager without code deployment (PRC-36, PRC-52)
- Per currency, the system stores the **conversion approach**: (a) Base RRP, (b) Fixed Pricelist from AP21, (c) Fixed FX rate from base, or (d) Dynamic FX rate from base (PRC-37)
- **Nightly job** loads Global-e pricing into SFCC: FX rates, price coefficients, and rounding rules (PRC-38)
- Pricebooks generated from Global-e pricing data and imported into SFCC (PRC-39)
- Target-currency price calculation: `base pricebook price × FX rate × country coefficient × product-class coefficient` (PRC-40)
- Calculated prices included in the SFCC search index for price-based filters and sort on PLP/search (PRC-41)
- All promotion calculations executed in the customer's selected ship-to currency (PRC-42)
- **Currency display formatting** per locale: symbol position, decimal places (including zero-decimal currencies), thousand separator, minus-sign for refunds (PRC-47)
- **FX rate locked at order placement** and applied to any refund at the same locked rate — refund in target currency equals original charged amount (PRC-48)
- **Currency rounding strategy** per currency (e.g. nearest whole AED, 2 decimal EUR, 0 decimal JPY); applied at line-item level before tax/promotion stacking (PRC-49)
- Business Manager interface for authorised users: view conversion approach per currency, set/change conversion approach, view current FX rate with last-updated timestamp and feed status; read-only access for merchandising team (PRC-50)
- Bulk import/export of currency config via SFCC Site Import/Export, OCAPI, or deployment scripts — technical users only (PRC-51)

---

## 5. VIC & Customer Group Pricing (PRC-17 – PRC-19)

Customer-group-specific catalogue pricing — visible on PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended tiles, wishlist (not cart-only discounts). Discounts do not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards.

| Customer group | Discount |
|---|---|
| Gold VIC | Permanent 10% off all non-sale products |
| Platinum VIC | Permanent discount — rate TBC (Zimmermann to confirm) |
| VIC early access | Flat 30% off before public sale goes live; removed before public sale |
| Advent customers | e.g. 50% off during Advent events |
| PR companies and investors | Configured discount |

- **Customer group discounts do NOT stack on sale items** (PRC-18, revised per DR): sale items are excluded from promotion set-ups. Example: a Gold VIC customer receives 10% off full-price items, but if they add a sale product to cart they get the sale price only — no extra 10% on top. The system must continue to support this exclusion.
- Configurable priority rules in SFCC Business Manager (e.g. Gold VIC 10% excludes gift cards and items already on sale) (PRC-19)

---

## 6. Global-e Pricing & Cart Handoff (PRC-15 – PRC-16, PRC-43 – PRC-46, PRC-53 – PRC-55)

- DDP/DDU duties messaging on PDP per country — configurable per country (PRC-15)
- SFCC passes a **complete cart to Global-e** in the customer's target currency at international checkout, including: all line items with quantities, prices in target currency, all applied promotions and coupon codes, Retail Rewards, gift cards, and a placeholder/dummy shipping method. Global-e adds actual shipping charges and processes payment (PRC-16, PRC-43). Note (DR): current M2 implementation has limitations — Global-e does not accept M2 catalogue promotions where the discount price appears on PLP/PDP for logged-in customer groups. Open (25.05): confirm with Global-e whether the SFCC cartridge supports honouring customer-group catalogue prices at Global-e checkout; if not currently honoured in M2, Zimmermann to confirm how these VIC/customer-group customers are receiving their discounts at international checkout today (e.g. configured directly in Global-e).
- **Coupon codes**: validation occurs in SFCC; discount values passed to Global-e in cart payload — Global-e does not call back to SFCC to re-validate (PRC-46, open — workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off comment conditions delivery on Global-e being able to apply and validate coupons: "This will be delivered only if Global-e can support." Treated as open until Global-e confirms capability; see Open Items)
- **Gift card webhooks**: GiveX gift card validate/redeem/refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44)
- **Retail Rewards at Global-e checkout**: applied after promotions (PRC-45, open — RJ challenges the "max 1 reward per order" limit: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order". Max-rewards-per-order count to be confirmed; see Open Items)
- Customers can purchase GiveX gift cards as products at Global-e checkout; provisioned in GiveX via existing middleware after payment (PRC-53, confirmed). Note (RJ): for Global-e regions gift cards are digital-only; currency coverage to be confirmed — see Open Items
- **Daily Global-e catalogue export job**: generates and uploads a product catalogue CSV to Global-e via SFTP for product-level restrictions, VAT rates, and HS code assignments (PRC-54)
- Authentication configured between SFCC and Global-e for all API calls (PRC-55)

---

## 7. Open Items

- RetailPrice functional confirmation owner outstanding (EK query) — assumption is RetailPrice stored as an additional SFCC price field (PRC-01)
- Final sale vs. is_returnable attribute distinction and AP21 derivation — Zimmermann to confirm; no final-sale icon in design yet (PRC-12, otherwise confirmed)
- AP21 MarkdownStatus values (permanent / temporary / temppermanent) and storefront behaviour — Zimmermann to confirm (PRC-13)
- Platinum VIC permanent discount rate — TBC (PRC-17)
- Fixed pricelists once imported via MuleSoft — CS query: confirm in-system accessibility vs. today's SFTP append (PRC-35, otherwise confirmed)
- **Coupon codes at Global-e checkout** — workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off comment is conditional: "RJ / Mani need to confirm that the coupon can be applied and is validated through Global-e. This will be delivered only if Global-e can support." Confirm with Global-e that the SFCC cartridge can apply and validate coupon codes before this requirement is treated as confirmed (PRC-46)
- Global-e SFCC cartridge support for customer-group catalogue prices at international checkout (PRC-43) — confirm with Global-e; Zimmermann to confirm current M2 workaround for VIC pricing at Global-e checkout
- Retail Rewards count at Global-e checkout — requirement states max 1 reward per order; RJ challenges: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order". Confirm max-per-order before implementing (PRC-45)

# PR #118 review — contract fidelity & house-rule conformance of the two new overrides

Rubric read at base `63855e6e`. **Note on the brief:** `.claude/rules/overrides.md` **does not exist** at base or head — it only ever lived on `feature/f2r-component-registry` (commits `3b340a59`/`a6842cf1`, 2026-08-14) and never merged. `overrideStyling.md` links to it 6 times; every one of those links is dangling. I judged against `overrideStyling.md`'s own "Importing an already-overridden component…" and "SFCC bridge pattern" sections instead.

## Gates I re-ran (all reproduce your numbers exactly)

| Gate | Base | Head | My verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | ✅ exit 0 |
| `vitest run` | — | 107 files / 1551 tests pass | ✅ identical |
| `eslint overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}` | 1297 | 1821 | ✅ identical; **+522 `prettier/prettier`, +1 `no-non-null-assertion`, +1 unused-disable-directive** |
| `auditTokenUsage.mjs` | 6 | 11 | ✅ identical; **all 5 new ones are verbatim SFCC carry-overs** |

Method: exported both trees with `git archive` into the scratchpad and ran the repo's own binaries against them, so nothing read the working tree.

---

## F1 — BLOCKING. The base-path import means `order-summary` renders the **base** `item-price` in *every* environment, including the shipped app — and that fails a named AC

`overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx:29`
```ts
import CartItemVariantPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price'
```

**Rule:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` § "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" — import B via a relative path, not the SFCC base path.

**The doc understates this, and I verified the resolver directly** rather than trusting either the doc or a source read. I instantiated the real `OverridesResolverPlugin` (`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`) exactly as `configs/webpack/config.js:151-156` does, pointed it at the PR-head tree, and replayed the actual request:

| Issuer | Request | Resolves to |
|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/order-summary/` | base path → item-price | **BASE `node_modules` .jsx** |
| `node_modules/.../order-summary/` | base path → item-price | override `.tsx` |
| `node_modules/.../checkout/` | base path → order-summary | override `.tsx` |

The cause is `isFromExtends()`'s second condition, `!filepath.includes(issuerPath)` — the redirect is **deliberately skipped when the issuer is inside `overrides/`**, and the plugin's own comment says so: *"This will return false if the issuer is a file in the overrides dir… allows the overrides to import from the base template using the same syntax."*

So the answer to your question 1 is: **none of the three resolve to the override.** Not the real app build, not `.storybook/main.js` (which aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` → `node_modules`, no resolver), not `vitest.config.ts` (no alias for that package at all). `overrideStyling.md`'s claim that a base-path import "will build and run correctly in the shipped app" is **wrong** — worth a separate doc fix, since it would let the next person make this exact mistake believing only Storybook/Vitest were affected.

**What the PR's own test and story actually exercise: neither component's new code.** Both files leave `showCartItems` at its `false` default, so `CartItems` — the only thing that renders `CartItemVariantPrice` — never mounts. Proven with coverage rather than by reading: `vitest run overrides/app/components/order-summary --coverage.all=false` produces **no coverage entry for `item-variant/item-price.tsx` at all** (the module is never even loaded), and `order-summary/index.tsx` itself sits at **50.48% statements (155/307)**.
